title: Rigveda 7.57: To the Maruts
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.57: To the Maruts: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.57 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to the Maruts. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 529r-529v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.57.1-5 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 4, varga 27); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 529r
translation.original_text:
1madhvo̍ vo̱ nāma̱ māru̍taṁ yajatrā̱ḥ pra ya̱jñeṣu̱ śava̍sā madanti | ye re̱jaya̍nti̱ roda̍sī cid u̱rvī pinva̱nty utsa̱ṁ yad ayā̍sur u̱grāḥ ||
2ni̱ce̱tāro̱ hi ma̱ruto̍ gṛ̱ṇanta̍m praṇe̱tāro̱ yaja̍mānasya̱ manma̍ | a̱smāka̍m a̱dya vi̱dathe̍ṣu ba̱rhir ā vī̱taye̍ sadata pipriyā̱ṇāḥ ||
3naitāva̍d a̱nye ma̱ruto̱ yathe̱me bhrāja̍nte ru̱kmair āyu̍dhais ta̱nūbhi̍ḥ | ā roda̍sī viśva̱piśa̍ḥ piśā̱nāḥ sa̍mā̱nam a̱ñjy a̍ñjate śu̱bhe kam ||
4ṛdha̱k sā vo̍ maruto di̱dyud a̍stu̱ yad va̱ āga̍ḥ puru̱ṣatā̱ karā̍ma | mā va̱s tasyā̱m api̍ bhūmā yajatrā a̱sme vo̍ astu suma̱tiś cani̍ṣṭhā ||
5kṛ̱te ci̱d atra̍ ma̱ruto̍ raṇantānava̱dyāsa̱ḥ śuca̍yaḥ pāva̱kāḥ | pra ṇo̍ 'vata suma̱tibhi̍r yajatrā̱ḥ pra vāje̍bhis tirata pu̱ṣyase̍ naḥ ||
translation.text:
1YEA, through the power of your sweet juice, ye Holy! the Marut host is glad at sacrifices. They cause even spacious heaven and earth to tremble, they make the spring flow when they come, the Mighty.
2The Maruts watch the man who sings their praises, promoters of the thought of him who worships. Seat you on sacred grass in our assembly, this day, with friendly minds, to share the banquet.
3No others gleam so brightly as these Maruts with their own forms, their golden gauds, their weapons. With all adornments, decking earth and heaven, they heighten, for bright show, their common splendour.
4Far from us be your blazing dart, O Maruts, when we, through human frailty, sin against you. Let us not he exposed to that, ye Holy! May your most loving favour still attend us.
5May even what we have done delight the Maruts, the blameless Ones, the bright, the purifying. Further us, O ye Holy, with your kindness: advance us mightily that we may prosper.

translation.original_ref: RV 7.57.6-7 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 4, varga 27); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 529v
translation.original_text:
6u̱ta stu̱tāso̍ ma̱ruto̍ vyantu̱ viśve̍bhi̱r nāma̍bhi̱r naro̍ ha̱vīṁṣi̍ | dadā̍ta no a̱mṛta̍sya pra̱jāyai̍ jigṛ̱ta rā̱yaḥ sū̱nṛtā̍ ma̱ghāni̍ ||
7ā stu̱tāso̍ maruto̱ viśva̍ ū̱tī acchā̍ sū̱rīn sa̱rvatā̍tā jigāta | ye na̱s tmanā̍ śa̱tino̍ va̱rdhaya̍nti yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text:
6And may the Maruts, praised by all their titles, Heroes, enjoy the taste of our oblations. Give us of Amrit for the sake of offspring: awake the excellent fair stores of riches.
7Hither, ye Maruts, praised, with all your succours, with all felicity come to our princes, Who, of themselves, a hundredfold increase us. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
